chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property directly matches the relation phrase's meaning, indicating the subject matter of an entity. The broad domain of 'Thing' allows for compatibility with various subject types, including CreativeWork and Event.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage
candidates.comment: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: identifyingTest

candidates.label: studySubject

candidates.label: typicalTest
candidates.comment: A typical test relation between a medical condition and a medical test commonly performed for that condition. Also called common test, diagnostic test, standard test. candidates.label: trialDesign

candidates.label: availableTest
candidates.comment: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by a diagnostic lab. Also called: lab test, diagnostic offering, test procedure. Examples: "DiagnosticLab 'LabCorp' availableTest 'Blood Test'", "DiagnosticLab 'Imaging Center' availableTest 'MRI Scan'."

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: identifyingExam
candidates.comment: An identifying exam relation between a medical sign and a physical examination that can detect it. Also called diagnostic exam, detection exam, exam for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying exam of a neurological check.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying exam.", "This sign requires an identifying exam."

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

relations.definition: Indicates participation or inclusion in an event or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: involves: Indicates participation or inclusion in an event or activity.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: participant

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

relations.embedding_query_text: isHeadquartersOf:

chosen_property.label: isHeadquartersFor
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the organization for which a building serves as the headquarters.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures the inverse of 'schema.org:headquarters' for 'Building -> Organization'. Minting 'isHeadquartersFor' provides this specific semantic.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

candidates.label: alternativeHeadline
candidates.comment: An alternative headline relation between a creative work and its secondary title. Also called subtitle, secondary title, sub-headline. Examples: "A news article's alternative headline is 'Local Hero Saves Cat'.", "A book's alternative headline is 'A Novel of Intrigue'."

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: masthead
candidates.comment: A masthead relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL listing its top editorial management. Also called: editorial board, management list, staff directory. Examples: "The New York Times masthead 'About Us' page", "BBC News masthead Editorial Leadership", "Local Newspaper masthead 'Our Team' section".

candidates.label: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
candidates.comment: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: isUnlabelledFallback
candidates.comment: A default setting relation indicating whether delivery time or shipping rate settings serve as a general fallback for unlabelled shipping details. Also called default settings, fallback rule, general application, unlabelled default. Examples: DeliveryTimeSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. ShippingRateSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. These settings are isUnlabelledFallback for all products.

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

relations.definition: Indicates the function or position held by an individual.
relations.embedding_query_text: hasRole: Indicates the function or position held by an individual.

instances: Dr Samuel Roger Kamba -> Health Minister

chosen_property.label: jobTitle
chosen_property.justification: The 'jobTitle' property directly captures the meaning of 'function or position held by an individual' as a 'formal designation within an organization'.

candidates.label: chemicalRole
candidates.comment: A functional relation describing the role played by a chemical substance or molecular entity within a chemical context. Also called "chemical function", "biochemical role", "molecular role". Examples: "Enzyme chemical role 'Catalyst'", "Drug chemical role 'Agonist'".

candidates.label: biologicalRole
candidates.comment: A defined term describing the role played by a biochemical entity within a biological context. Also called: biological function, physiological role, molecular role. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Enzyme' biologicalRole 'Catalyst'", "BioChemEntity 'Hormone' biologicalRole 'Signaling Molecule'."

candidates.label: educationalRole
candidates.comment: An educational role relation between an educational audience and the text describing its specific role. Also called "audience role", "learner role", "student type". Examples: "Educational audience educationalRole 'Student'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Teacher'", "Educational audience educationalRole 'Parent'".

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: position
candidates.comment: An ordinal attribute indicating the sequential position of an item within a series or list. Also called order, rank, sequence number, index. Examples: A list item has a position of '1'. A chapter in a book has a position of 'Chapter 3'. A search result has a position of '5'.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: hasMolecularFunction
candidates.comment: A molecular function relation between a biochemical entity and its performed molecular function. Also called performs function, molecular role, functional activity. Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

relations.embedding_query_text: of: Indicates possession, belonging, or association.

chosen_property.justification: A government organization is located in or operates within a country. 'location' is a suitable property for this.

instances: Health Minister -> Democratic Republic of Congo

chosen_property.label: roleInCountry
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the country in which an organization role is held or applies.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures the relationship of an 'OrganizationRole' being 'of' a 'Country'. Minting 'roleInCountry' provides this specific semantic.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Indicates the starting point or initial event of a process or sequence.
relations.embedding_query_text: beganWith: Indicates the starting point or initial event of a process or sequence.

chosen_property.label: subEvent
chosen_property.justification: The 'subEvent' property accurately captures the meaning of one event being the starting point or component of a larger event.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. candidates.label: pageStart
candidates.comment: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: "Article X pageStart 135", "Chapter Y pageStart 'xiii'", "Report Z pageStart 1". Distinct from pageEnd, which is the concluding page. pagination is a general range.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: tripOrigin
candidates.comment: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

candidates.label: jobStartDate
candidates.comment: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

relations.definition: Indicates the entity that formally announced or proclaimed something.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. candidates.label: announcementLocation

candidates.label: recognizedBy

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

relations.definition: Indicates the outcome or consequence of an event or action.
relations.embedding_query_text: resultedIn: Indicates the outcome or consequence of an event or action.

chosen_property.label: caused
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that one quantity led to or caused another quantity.

candidates.label: result

candidates.label: resultComment

Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: possibleComplication

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: source

relations.embedding_query_text: toLocation: Indicates the destination or endpoint of a movement or transfer.

chosen_property.label: toLocation
chosen_property.justification: The 'toLocation' property directly matches the relation phrase and definition. 'TransportationEvent' can be considered a type of 'TransferAction' (a subtype of 'Action'), and 'City' is a 'Place'.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."

candidates.label: serviceLocation
candidates.comment: The physical place where a service can be accessed or obtained. Also called service access point, physical service location, service venue. Examples: `Bank Service Channel` serviceLocation `Bank Branch`, `Government Service Channel` serviceLocation `City Hall`, `Repair Service Channel` serviceLocation `Repair Shop`. Distinct from `serviceArea`, which is the broader geographic region.

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

chosen_property.justification: The 'fromLocation' property directly matches the relation phrase and definition. 'TransportationEvent' and 'EscapeEvent' are types of 'Action', and 'State'/'MedicalClinic' are 'Place's.

candidates.label: tripOrigin

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."
